A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LACING and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Retained content can be matched across renumbering and relocation, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark experiments with 7B and 13B models, component ablations, attention analyses, parameter studies, and human evaluation.

after.justification: V2 retains these empirical results and adds benchmark evaluations, LLaVA-NeXT experiments, additional controls, FFN-only tuning results, and early-fusion model analyses.

M1.justification: The primary MDA/SIG architecture, training loss, and decoding rule remain unchanged. V2 Section E.6 introduces an optional FFN-only fine-tuning procedure instead of full-model retraining, providing a limited procedural extension.

E1.justification: V2 adds actual evaluations on ScienceQA, POPE, SeedBench, and MMVP in Table 7, substantially extending the retained benchmark coverage. Section F additionally evaluates ScienceQA questions requiring images versus questions not requiring images.

E2.justification: ICD becomes an evaluated comparator in Table 1 at both model sizes, having only been cited in v1. New Table 9 expands SIG comparisons to IBD, ICD, VDD-UNK, and a blank-image variant, substantially broadening the previous VCD/VDD-None comparisons.

E3.justification: V2 introduces LLaVA-NeXT training and evaluation, causal-attention and blank-image controls, FFN-only tuning, and ScienceQA evaluation stratified by image requirement. These extend the experimental design; the original LLaVA-1.5 hyperparameters, GPT-4 evaluator specification, and human-study procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Sections E–F add learned-versus-blank prompt comparisons, causal-versus-bidirectional attention tests, 13B component ablations, FFN-only tuning comparisons, and early-fusion analyses. The original 7B MMBench ablation column is removed. Existing parameter studies, human evaluation, case studies, and attention-map comparisons are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The retained attention averaging and three-person human-evaluation procedure do not introduce a changed uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Original headline results remain, including Table 1's LACING LLaVABench scores of 72.20 and 84.30, while substantial new benchmark and control results are added and 7B MMBench ablation entries disappear. New Table 13 reports 68.99 for greedy 13B w/o MDA on MMBench, versus 70.19 for SIG in v1 Table 2 and retained v2 Table 10. Without reconciled settings, this is not an established same-setting performance change.

T1.justification: The attention-mask definitions, dual-attention equations, Bayesian derivation, and guided-logit formula in Equations 1–10 are mathematically unchanged. V2 adds no substantive formal assumptions, proofs, or theoretical results.

C1.justification: V2's abstract and introduction explicitly extend the empirical generality claim to different model architectures, supported by the added LLaVA-NeXT experiment. The two proposed sources of language bias, MDA/SIG contributions, and headline improvement claims remain essentially unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations concerning early fusion, gains from causal MDA, FFN-only practicality, and possible overfitting behind RLHF-V's advantage on object hallucination. Limitations now emphasize unavailable alignment data for newer architectures. V1's explanation of SIG alone outperforming full LACING on 7B MMBench is removed.

D1.justification: V2 adds the Open-LLaVA-NeXT training-data source and backbone details, plus the reported FFN-only trainable budget of approximately 500M parameters. Original hardware and hyperparameter disclosures remain. The code/model statement changes from already available to a future release; actual availability cannot be established from the PDFs.

R1.justification: V2 explicitly grounds SIG in classifier-free guidance and distinguishes MDA from shared-attention approaches in Show-o and Transfusion. It also incorporates encoder-free and early-fusion models, FFN knowledge-editing work, and newer multimodal literature, substantially expanding the positioning of the method.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and experimental discussion undergo extensive rewriting. Limitations move from the appendix into main Section 6, additional analysis subsections are introduced, and the appendix is reorganized with an added related-work section. Author information and citation style also change.

P2.justification: V2 adds several experimental tables, redraws Figure 2 to include EVE, and adds the Chameleon attention plot. Original Table 2 is split between main Table 2 and appendix Table 10, while Table 4 loses its MMBench column. Table styling, figure placement, typography, and page layout are extensively revised.

improvement.justification: The new blank-image and attention-direction controls better substantiate the design choices, while additional benchmarks and LLaVA-NeXT testing broaden validation. These provide a limited net improvement over v1. Benefits are tempered by incomplete details for some new experiments, unreconciled 13B ablation values, and removal of the explicit 7B MMBench component tradeoff.
